---
title: "tsmom-band"
subtitle: "Cost-aware time-series momentum on a $20 IBKR account"
date: 2026-04-01
---

::: {.status}
Currently paper trading. The code is on [GitHub](https://github.com/NavyBlueCheese/tsmom-band).
:::

Long-or-flat time-series momentum across four ETFs (SPY, EFA, IEF, GLD),
sized for a cash account of about $20 at Interactive Brokers. At that
size IBKR's commission cap of 1% of trade value applies to every order,
so a round trip costs 2% of the position. Most of the design is about
not giving that money away.

**The rules**, fixed in a preregistration before any backtest was run:

- **Signal:** the sign of the 21-to-252-day return, per asset. Long or flat, never short.
- **Sizing:** inverse volatility from a 60-day Ledoit–Wolf shrunk covariance, 15% annual volatility target, no leverage.
- **Rebalance:** last trading session of each quarter, 15:45 New York time.
- **No-trade band:** a leg only trades if its target weight differs from the current weight by more than 0.20.
- **Costs:** IBKR Pro's tiered US-stock schedule, plus SEC and FINRA fees on sells.

None of these get tuned to make a backtest look better. Parameter sweeps
are logged as trials and the defaults stay where they are.

**The prediction.** Before the account was funded, a block bootstrap of
the training-period backtest predicted one-year P&L of about +$0.85, with
an 80% interval of −$0.26 to +$2.37 and roughly 1.6 trades a year. The
point of the project is calibration: does the live result land inside
that interval?

**How it's built.** Everything runs through an event-driven engine that
only ever sees data up to the current bar, so lookahead is impossible by
construction. The same strategy code runs in backtest and live. Money
amounts use exact decimals, data from 2019 onward is a sealed holdout
with a committed hash, and six kill-switch conditions each need a human
to clear them.

The paper-trading runner is currently doing its weekly cycles.
